title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 — Phase 65 GSA post-quantum acquisition review
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the GSA post-quantum acquisition reporting pack. NIST CSF 2.0 provides a voluntary taxonomy of high-level cybersecurity outcomes for organizations of any size, sector, or maturity, with expanded governance and supply-chain emphasis.
key_findings: CSF 2.0 is designed for all organizations rather than only critical-infrastructure operators.
The update adds stronger governance and supply-chain emphasis and organizes outcomes through six functions, including the new Govern function.
NIST states that the framework does not prescribe how outcomes must be achieved and instead links users to implementation resources, profiles, and informative references.
why_it_matters: Which records move a migration obligation through inventory, solicitation, award, interoperability test, cutover, acceptance, rollback, and legacy retirement? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. CSF 2.0 supplies a common outcome vocabulary for connecting policy, organizational governance, sector profiles, controls, and implementation evidence.
ftfn_relevance: Provides a stable organizing layer for Cybersecurity and Policy and Standards.
Supports crosswalks between CISA goals, NIST publications, operator controls, and evidence requests.
Clarifies that framework alignment and implemented safeguards are separate evidence stages.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The framework is voluntary unless another authority makes it binding.
Use, mapping, or claimed alignment does not prove implementation effectiveness or reduced risk.
The high-level outcome taxonomy does not replace sector, system, asset, control, or incident evidence.
